title: Constructible stable locus and dense isomorphism open for a spread modification
statement: Let $U_0$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $\mathbf Z$ with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta_0$, let $L$ be a separable closure of $k(U_0)$, and let $V$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$ together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_0$ whose restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ lies over $\eta_0$, i.e. a point $x$ of $RZ_L(U_0)$ as in [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement] (with $U_0$ in place of $T$). Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $U_0$-curve whose fibre $X_{\eta_0}$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and whose fibre $D_{\eta_0}$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $k(U_0)$, let $(Y_0,E_0)$ be a multipointed $U_0$-curve, and let $g_X:Y_0\to X$, $g_D:E_0\to D$ be a compatible pair of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] which are isomorphisms on the fibres over $\eta_0$. Assume that the pullback of $(g_X,g_D)$ along $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a stable $\eta$-modification of $(X,D)\times_{U_0}\operatorname{Spec}V$. Then there are an $L$-quasi-model $U\to U_0$ in the sense of [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement] and a factorization $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U\to U_0$ compatible with the maps from $\operatorname{Spec}L$ (so $x\in RZ_L(U)$) such that the pullback $(Y_0,E_0)\times_{U_0}U\to(X,D)\times_{U_0}U$ is a stable $\eta$-modification over $U$, and there is a dense open $U^\circ\subseteq U$ containing the generic point of $U$ such that both pulled-back maps are isomorphisms over the preimages of $U^\circ$. This is the constructibility of the semistable and stable fibre loci together with the openness of the isomorphism locus; no modification over $V$ is constructed. Here a multipointed curve $(Z,F)$ over a scheme $S$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $Z\to S$, $F\to S$ of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$ (every irreducible component of every fibre has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] $1$, resp. $0$) and a closed immersion $F\hookrightarrow Z$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] over $S$; $F$ may be empty and $Z$ need not be separated or proper over $S$. A pair of morphisms $Z'\to Z$, $F'\to F$ of multipointed curves is compatible when it commutes with the two closed immersions. For an integral base $S$ with generic point $\xi$ and a multipointed $S$-curve $(Z,F)$, an $\eta$-modification of $(Z,F)$ is a multipointed $S$-curve $(Z',F')$ with a compatible pair $Z'\to Z$, $F'\to F$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on the fibre over $\xi$; here an open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_W$ is injective. $(Z',F')$ is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $Z'$ has completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] over its algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$, $F'\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $F'$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A semistable $\eta$-modification is stable if no geometric fibre of $Z'$ has an irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $Z'\to Z$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of that fibre in at most two points.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), Remark 3.1.1(ii), and the second paragraph of the proof of Theorem 1.5, pp. 34--36 (constructibility of stable fibres and shrinking to the stable locus).

proof.text: First obtain an isomorphism open on the original base. All four schemes $X,D,Y_0,E_0$ are of finite presentation over $U_0$, by the multipointed hypotheses. Choose any nonempty affine open $A\subseteq U_0$. The principal opens $D(a)\subseteq A$ for nonzero $a\in\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$ form a directed inverse system with affine transitions and limit $\operatorname{Spec}k(U_0)$: its coordinate-ring colimit is the fraction field of the domain $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$. Use [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) to descend the two given generic inverse maps, and (3) to impose both inverse identities for each map after a common further localization. This yields a nonempty open $W_0\subseteq A\subseteq U_0$ containing $\eta_0$ over whose full preimages both $g_X$ and $g_D$ are isomorphisms. Also $U_0$ and all its finite-type quasi-models are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. No valuation-centre descent theorem is used to spread these generic inverses.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (2),(3), applied to principal open neighbourhoods of the generic point; Morphisms Tag 01T6.

proof.text: The open $W_0$ is schematically dense in $U_0$: every affine domain $B$ in the integral scheme injects into $k(U_0)$, so a section vanishing on $W_0$ vanishes at the generic point and is zero on each such affine chart. The open immersion $W_0\hookrightarrow U_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since $U_0$ is Noetherian. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] with this immersion as $h$ and first $q:X\to U_0$, then $q:D\to U_0$. Both are flat by hypothesis. The inverse images $X_{W_0}\subseteq X$ and $D_{W_0}\subseteq D$ are therefore schematically dense in the targets of $g_X$ and $g_D$. Together with properness and the generic isomorphisms, Step 1 shows that $g$ is an $\eta$-modification. This step does not assert semistability of $(Y_0,E_0)$.

source.place: Tag 081I (flat base change of scheme-theoretic images), with the flat target maps X and D.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-stable-modification-constructibility] to the proper pair $g$ over the integral Noetherian base $U_0$. Its generic-isomorphism and dense-target-open assumptions were verified in Steps 1--2; its source need not yet be semistable. Let $C\subseteq U_0$ be the resulting constructible subset of points at which the source geometric fibre is semistable and has no exceptional contracted component. For every point $v\in\operatorname{Spec}V$, put $u=g_V(v)\in U_0$, where $g_V$ denotes the prescribed base map. The fibre of the pulled-back pair at $v$ is the base change of the pair at $u$ along the field extension $\kappa(u)\hookrightarrow\kappa(v)$. It is geometrically stable by the hypothesis on the modification over $V$. The reverse implication of [lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-field-descent] gives semistability and geometric stability at $u$. Thus the image of every point, not only the closed point, of $\operatorname{Spec}V$ lies in $C$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34, and the field-extension invariance hypothesis of Remark 3.1.1(i)(a),(ii), pp. 14--15.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $A_0\subseteq U_0$ containing the centre of $V$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_0$ factors through $A_0$, since every point of the spectrum of a local ring generalizes its closed point. The set $C_0=C\cap A_0$ is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction]. Since $A_0$ is Noetherian affine, write $C_0$ as a finite Boolean combination of principal opens, using [def-weil-constructible-subset] and finite principal-open covers of its open pieces. Consider the directed system of affine centred quasi-models $U_i\to A_0$, let $c_i$ be their centres, and put $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{U_i,c_i}$. By [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-local-colimit], its limit is $\operatorname{Spec}V$, also after restricting to refinements of $A_0$. All $T_i$ are affine, hence qcqs, and their transition maps are affine. The inverse image of $C_0$ in $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{A_0,c_0}$ is constructible: replace each principal open in the Boolean expression by the principal open of its image in this local ring. Step 3 says that the limit maps into this inverse image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] (05F4) to obtain an index $i$ for which the entire image of $T_i\to A_0$ is contained in $C_0$.

source.place: Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible), first application, along the centre local rings; Temkin Lemma 3.2.2, printed p. 16.

proof.text: Write the affine quasi-model just chosen as $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with centre $c_i$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p\subset B$. The subset $E_i\subseteq U_i$ which is the inverse image of $C_0$ is a finite Boolean combination of principal opens, by the same substitution of functions as in Step 4, so is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The limit of the directed system $D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}B_f$, indexed by $f\notin\mathfrak p$ and ordered by further localization, is $\operatorname{Spec}B_{\mathfrak p}$: $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is the colimit of these localizations. All stages and transition maps are affine. Step 4 says this limit maps into $E_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] a second time, now to these principal neighbourhoods (including $D(1)=U_i$). It gives $f\notin\mathfrak p$ with $U:=D(f)\subseteq E_i$. Since the map $B_{\mathfrak p}\to V$ is local, $f$ maps to a unit of $V$, and the chosen lift $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U_i$ factors through $U$. The scheme $U$ is integral, and its composite to $U_0$ is separated of finite type with the prescribed generic map from $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Thus it is an $L$-quasi-model through $x$ whose image in $U_0$ is contained in $C$.

source.place: Tag 05F4, second application, along principal affine neighbourhoods of the chosen centre; the localization colimit is written out.

proof.text: Pull back the given pairs to $U$, writing them as $(Y,E)\to(X_U,D_U)$. By [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change], both remain multipointed curves, and the target retains its smooth generic curve and etale generic marking because the generic point maps to $\eta_0$. Properness of each pair map follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. For any $t\in U$ with image $s\in C$, the pair over $\kappa(t)$ is the base change of the pair over $\kappa(s)$. By [lem-trf-stable-modification-stability-field-descent], it is semistable and geometrically stable. In particular $E_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is etale. Flatness and finite presentation of $E\to U$ allow [lem-sbc-flat-fibre-etale-neighbourhoods] at each $t$, proving that $E\to U$ is etale. At every point of $E$ the fibre curve is smooth; flatness and finite presentation of $Y\to U$ allow [lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion], so the marking lies in the relative smooth locus. The nodal geometric fibres and absence of exceptional components already hold at every $t$. Hence the source over $U$ is semistable and has the geometric stability condition of the item.

source.place: §1.2, printed p. 2: semistability is equivalent to semistability on geometric fibres; arbitrary base change and Remark 3.1.1.

proof.text: Set $U^\circ=U\times_{U_0}W_0$. It is an open containing the generic point of the integral scheme $U$, so is dense and schematically dense by the affine-domain argument of Step 2. The maps over its full preimages are isomorphisms by Step 1 and transitivity of fibre products. Because $U$ is Noetherian, the open immersion $U^\circ\hookrightarrow U$ is qcqs. Apply [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback] to this immersion and the flat maps $X_U\to U$ and $D_U\to U$. This proves schematic density in the two targets $X_U$ and $D_U$, including when the marking is empty. With properness from Step 6 and the generic-fibre isomorphisms, the pair is an $\eta$-modification; Step 6 makes it stable. Finally the factorization from Step 5 respects $\operatorname{Spec}L$, so [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement] identifies its point of $RZ_L(U)$ with $x$ under the open injection into $RZ_L(U_0)$. This is every conclusion of the item.

lean.statement: theorem stable_modification_stability_locus (U₀ : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral U₀] (t₀ : U₀ ⟶ Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) [LocallyOfFiniteType t₀] [QuasiCompact t₀] (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra U₀.functionField L] [IsSepClosure U₀.functionField L] (x : RiemannZariski.ValuationPoint U₀ L (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀))) (X Y₀ : MultipointedCurve U₀) (g : Y₀.Hom X) [IsProper g.curve] [IsProper g.marking] (hX : Smooth (pullback.snd X.x (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀)))) (hD : Etale (pullback.snd X.d (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀)))) (hηcurve : IsIso (g.curveBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀)))) (hηmark : IsIso (g.markingBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀)))) (hV : ∃ (P' : Y₀.BaseChange x.centre) (Q' : X.BaseChange x.centre) (f' : MultipointedCurve.BaseChangeHom g x.centre P' Q'), f'.hom.IsStable (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom x.V.subtype)) ∧ IsProper f'.hom.curve ∧ IsProper f'.hom.marking) : ∃ (U : RiemannZariski.QuasiModel U₀ L (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap U₀.functionField L)) ≫ U₀.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint U₀))) (l : Spec (.of x.V) ⟶ U.X), l ≫ U.map = x.centre ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom x.V.subtype) ≫ l = U.generic ∧ ∃ (P' : Y₀.BaseChange U.map) (Q' : X.BaseChange U.map) (f' : MultipointedCurve.BaseChangeHom g U.map P' Q'), f'.hom.IsStable U.generic ∧ ∃ V : U.X.Opens, genericPoint U.X ∈ V ∧ IsIso (f'.hom.curveBaseChange V.ι) ∧ IsIso (f'.hom.markingBaseChange V.ι)
